1	# solo06 - Multi-Tenant Content-Addressed Object Store
2	
3	This repository is a small but real backend skeleton for multi-tenant object
4	storage with content addressing. Every object key maps to the SHA-256 digest of
5	its bytes, blobs are written once under `<data-dir>/blobs/<sha256>` so identical
6	payloads are deduplicated no matter how many keys reference them, and object
7	metadata is kept in `<data-dir>/index.json` and rewritten atomically (temporary
8	file plus `os.replace`) so a crash never leaves a half-written index behind. The
9	same core is exposed three ways: as a Python API (`ContentAddressedStore`), as a
10	standard-library HTTP service, and as a command line tool. It uses only the
11	Python standard library, needs no network access and behaves deterministically,
12	which makes it a suitable frozen baseline for later work on chunked and
13	resumable uploads, object versioning and retention, lifecycle and garbage
14	collection, metadata indexing and listing, quotas and rate limiting, consistent
15	hashing and rebalancing, erasure coding and repair, signed URLs and access
16	control, cross-region replication and end-to-end audit.
17	
18	## Requirements
19	
20	* Python 3.10 or newer (developed and verified on Python 3.12).
21	* No third-party packages, no network access required.
22	
23	## Usage
24	
25	Start the HTTP server (run from the repository root):
26	
27	```
28	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
29	```
30	
31	The server prints one line of JSON before it starts serving, for example
32	`{"addr":"127.0.0.1:8080","data_dir":"/abs/path/objstore_data","ok":true}`, and
33	then runs until it receives SIGINT or SIGTERM.
34	
35	Store and fetch data over HTTP:
36	
37	```
38	printf 'hello' | curl -sS -X PUT --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
39	  http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects/a.txt
40	curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects/a.txt
41	curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects?prefix=&limit=100'
42	```
43	
44	Upload a large payload through a resumable HTTP session:
45	
46	```
47	size=$(wc -c < big.bin)
48	digest=$(sha256sum big.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
49	session=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads \
50	  -d "{\"key\":\"docs/big.bin\",\"size\":$size,\"sha256\":\"$digest\"}" \
51	  | sed 's/.*"session":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1')
52	head -c 1048576 big.bin | curl -sS -X PUT \
53	  "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session?offset=0" --data-binary @-
54	tail -c +1048577 big.bin | curl -sS -X PUT \
55	  "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session?offset=1048576" --data-binary @-
56	curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session/complete"
57	```
58	
59	Use the command line interface instead of the server:
60	
61	```
62	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data put --key docs/a.txt --file ./a.txt
63	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data get --key docs/a.txt --out ./copy.txt
64	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data list --prefix docs/ --limit 100
65	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data delete --key docs/a.txt
66	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data gc
67	python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data gc --execute
68	```
69	
70	The global `--data-dir` option must appear before the subcommand; it defaults to
71	`./objstore_data`. `put`, `get`, `list` and `delete` also accept `--tenant`
72	(default `default`) to pick the tenant namespace. Every command prints exactly
73	one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0 on success, or prints one line of JSON
74	on stderr and exits non-zero on failure.
75	
76	Use the Python API directly:
77	
78	```python
79	from objstore import ContentAddressedStore
80	
81	store = ContentAddressedStore("./objstore_data")
82	entry = store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", content_type="text/plain")
83	payload, head = store.get("docs/a.txt")
84	page = store.list_objects(prefix="docs/", after=None, limit=100)
85	result = store.collect_garbage()              # preview only
86	store.collect_garbage(dry_run=False)          # actually delete
87	```
88	
89	### Tenants
90	
91	Every object key lives in a tenant namespace. Two tenants may use the same
92	key for independent objects: reads, writes, deletes, conditional writes and
93	listings of one tenant never see or affect another tenant's objects. Tenants
94	need no provisioning — a tenant exists as soon as it has objects or sessions,
95	and listing a tenant without objects returns an empty page. A tenant name is
96	1–64 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`, starting with a
97	letter or digit; anything else raises `ObjectStoreError("invalid tenant: ...")`
98	(Python), returns `400 {"error":"invalid tenant ..."}` (HTTP) or the usual
99	CLI failure line with a non-zero exit, and changes no data.
100	
101	The Python API takes an optional `tenant` keyword (default `"default"`) on
102	`put`, `get`, `head`, `delete`, `list_objects` and every upload-session
103	operation:
104	
105	```python
106	store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", tenant="acme")
107	payload, head = store.get("docs/a.txt", tenant="acme")
108	page = store.list_objects(prefix="docs/", tenant="acme")
109	session = store.begin_upload("docs/big.bin", size, digest, tenant="acme")
110	```
111	
112	The HTTP object and upload-session endpoints select the tenant through the
113	optional `X-Objstore-Tenant` request header (default `default`); a repeated
114	header or an invalid name returns `400 {"error":"invalid tenant ..."}` and
115	takes precedence over every other request error. The CLI commands `put`,
116	`get`, `list` and `delete` accept an optional `--tenant` flag.
117	
118	A conditional write compares only the digest of the key in the same tenant,
119	and an upload session belongs to the tenant fixed at creation: its status,
120	append, complete and abort operations must name that tenant, and a valid
121	session id of another tenant behaves exactly like an unknown session id
122	(`ObjectStoreError` / `404`) without revealing any state. Blobs stay global —
123	identical content is stored once across all tenants, `blob`/`blob_digests`
124	and `GET /v1/blobs/{sha256}` keep their global meaning, and garbage
125	collection only reclaims content no tenant references anymore. Directories
126	written by older versions (objects, sessions and completion records without
127	tenant information) belong to the `default` tenant after the upgrade.
128	
129	### Conditional writes
130	
131	`put`, `delete` and `begin_upload` take an optional keyword
132	`expected_sha256` that makes the write or delete an atomic compare-and-swap on
133	the target key's current digest:
134	
135	* omitted entirely keeps the original unconditional behaviour;
136	* an explicit `None` requires the key not to exist;
137	* a string of 64 lowercase hex digits requires the key to exist with exactly
138	  that metadata digest.
139	
140	Only that key's digest is compared; the content type and every other key are
141	irrelevant. Any other value raises
142	`ObjectStoreError("invalid precondition")`. When the condition does not hold,
143	the operation raises `ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")` and changes
144	neither the object nor (for uploads) the session progress or any blob; a
145	satisfied absent-condition `delete` still raises the usual
146	`ObjectStoreError("not found: ...")`. The check and the mutation are one
147	indivisible operation under the store lock, so two concurrent writes that
148	both expect the same old digest cannot both succeed.
149	
150	```python
151	store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", expected_sha256=None)          # create only
152	store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello!", expected_sha256=head["sha256"])  # CAS update
153	store.delete("docs/a.txt", expected_sha256=head["sha256"])      # delete if unchanged
154	```
155	
156	For a resumable session the condition passed to `begin_upload` is saved with
157	the session and is not checked while the session is created or appended to;
158	it is evaluated once, atomically with the publish, against the object's state
159	at completion time (after the length and hash checks pass). A failed
160	precondition leaves the confirmed bytes and the incomplete session in place,
161	so it can be completed again or aborted; the condition still applies after
162	reopening the data directory, while session files written by older versions
163	stay unconditional.
164	
165	### Resumable uploads
166	
167	Large or unreliable transfers can be uploaded in chunks through a persistent
168	session instead of a single `put`:
169	
170	```python
171	session = store.begin_upload("docs/big.bin", size, sha256_of_full_content,
172	                             content_type="application/octet-stream")
173	store.upload_status(session)          # {"key","size","sha256","content_type","offset","completed"}
174	store.append_upload(session, 0, first_chunk)      # returns the received length
175	store.append_upload(session, len(first_chunk), second_chunk)
176	entry = store.complete_upload(session)            # publishes, returns put metadata
177	store.abort_upload(session)                       # or drop the session entirely
178	```
179	
180	`begin_upload` validates the key and content type exactly like `put`, requires
181	a non-negative integer `size` (booleans excluded) and the 64 lowercase hex
182	digits of the full content's SHA-256, and returns a unique string session id.
183	Creating a session changes no object, and sessions with their confirmed
184	progress survive reopening the data directory. `append_upload` accepts the
185	same byte types as `put`: a new chunk must start exactly at the current end
186	and may not exceed the declared size; re-sending identical bytes fully inside
187	the received range succeeds without growing, while different bytes, chunks
188	overlapping the received end, gaps and empty chunks anywhere but at the end
189	all raise `ObjectStoreError`. `complete_upload` publishes the object only when
190	the received length and the SHA-256 of the full content match the declaration
191	(zero-byte objects included); until then the key keeps its old value and no
192	new blob appears. Appending after completion fails, repeating a completed
193	`complete_upload` returns the first result without overwriting later writes
194	or deletes of the key, and `abort_upload` removes the session (returning
195	`None`) without deleting any published object. An interrupted append leaves
196	either the old progress or a whole new chunk, and an interrupted complete
197	leaves either the old object or the fully published new one; after recovery
198	the `completed` flag always agrees with what was published. Sessions on the
199	same key are independent and publish in completion order. Garbage collection
200	never touches data needed by incomplete sessions; once a session completes or
201	is aborted, its blob follows the normal object-reference rules and the
202	completion record itself keeps nothing alive. The command line interface is
203	unchanged by this feature; the HTTP session surface is documented below.
204	
205	`collect_garbage(dry_run=True)` returns
206	`{"digests": [...], "bytes": <int>, "dry_run": <bool>}`: the digests sorted
207	lexicographically and the sum of the files' actual byte sizes (zero-byte
208	blobs included). A dry run reports the candidates and changes nothing;
209	`dry_run=False` deletes the candidates and reports what that call removed.
210	References are recomputed from the current index on every call, so content
211	still shared by any key is kept, while content orphaned by an overwrite, by
212	deleting the last reference, or never indexed at all is collectable. Only
213	regular files directly in `blobs/` whose names are 64 lowercase hex digits
214	are eligible; other names, temporary files, subdirectories and symlinks are
215	preserved and symlink targets are never followed. Unreferenced files are
216	deleted without validating their content, and missing or corrupted blobs
217	that are still referenced do not block other candidates. A non-boolean
218	`dry_run` raises `ObjectStoreError("invalid dry_run")`, and any scanning,
219	stating or deletion I/O failure raises `ObjectStoreError("gc io error")`; a
220	failed scan deletes nothing, and a failure mid-deletion leaves the completed
221	deletions in place so a retry collects the rest. Garbage collection runs
222	under the same lock as object reads and writes within one store instance.
223	
224	
225	## Tests
226	
227	```
228	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
229	```
230	
231	Run the command from the repository root so that `import objstore` resolves.
232	
233	## HTTP API
234	
235	Errors are always JSON: `{"error": "..."}`. Unknown keys return
236	`404 {"error":"not found"}`; a malformed digest returns
237	`400 {"error":"invalid sha256"}`; an out-of-range or non-numeric `limit`
238	returns `400 {"error":"invalid limit"}`; an unknown path returns
239	`404 {"error":"not found"}`. Object PUT/DELETE and `POST /v1/uploads` accept
240	conditional headers: `If-Match` must be a single double-quoted lowercase
241	digest (`If-Match: "<sha256>"`) requiring the key to hold that digest, and
242	`If-None-Match: *` requires the key to be absent. Both headers together, a
243	repeated header, or any other value returns
244	`400 {"error":"invalid precondition"}`; a condition that does not hold
245	returns `412 {"error":"precondition failed"}` without changing anything (an
246	absent-key `DELETE` still returns its `404 not found`). Request/body errors,
247	unknown sessions, and length/hash conflicts keep their usual status codes and
248	take precedence over the condition. Successful object GET and HEAD return an
249	`ETag` header holding the current digest in double quotes; no other success
250	response changes. Upload session conflicts (gaps, bytes past the
251	received end or the declared size, conflicting re-sends, empty chunks away
252	from the end, appending after completion, or completing with the wrong length
253	or hash) return `409` and never change progress or the target object; a
254	missing, non-integer or negative `Content-Length` on session creation or
255	chunk append returns `411 {"error":"length required"}`; a request carrying
256	`Transfer-Encoding` returns `400` and a body shorter than its declared
257	`Content-Length` also returns `400`. Every object GET and blob GET recomputes
258	the SHA-256 of the bytes actually on disk before serving them; object GET also
259	checks the byte count against the metadata `size`. A failed check returns
260	`500 {"error":"corrupted blob"}` with no object bytes, and an I/O error on an
261	existing blob returns `500 {"error":"blob io error"}`; upload session I/O
262	failures return `500 {"error":"upload io error"}`. Re-PUTting an object
263	whose digest file is corrupted restores that file atomically from the complete
264	request body, which also repairs every other key sharing that digest; HEAD,
265	listings and digest listings remain metadata-only and perform no content
266	checks.
267	
268	| Method | Path | Success | Error codes |
269	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
270	| GET | `/healthz` | 200 `{"ok": true}` | 405 |
271	| PUT | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 201 `{"key","sha256","size"}` on first store; 200 with the same body when the same bytes are stored again | 400 invalid key / invalid precondition, 411 missing Content-Length, 405, 412 precondition failed, 500 blob io error |
272	| GET | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 200 raw bytes, headers `Content-Type`, `X-Content-Sha256` and `ETag` (`"<sha256>"`) | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key, 405, 500 corrupted blob / blob io error |
273	| HEAD | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 200 no body, headers `Content-Length`, `X-Content-Sha256` and `ETag` | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key, 405 |
274	| DELETE | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 204 no body | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key / invalid precondition, 405, 412 precondition failed |
275	| GET | `/v1/objects?prefix=&after=&limit=` | 200 `{"items":[{"key","sha256","size","content_type"}],"next_after":<str or null>}` | 400 invalid limit, 400 invalid prefix, 400 invalid after, 405 |
276	| GET | `/v1/blobs/{sha256}` | 200 raw bytes of that content, header `X-Content-Sha256` | 400 invalid sha256, 404 unknown digest, 405, 500 corrupted blob / blob io error |
277	| POST | `/v1/uploads` | 201 `{"session":"<id>"}`; body is a UTF-8 JSON object with required `key`, `size`, `sha256` and optional `content_type` (default `null`); optional `If-Match`/`If-None-Match` save a publish-time condition | 400 invalid json / fields / invalid precondition, 411 missing/non-integer/negative Content-Length, 400 Transfer-Encoding / truncated body, 405, 500 upload io error |
278	| GET | `/v1/uploads/{session}` | 200 `{"key","size","sha256","content_type","offset","completed"}` | 404 unknown or aborted session, 405 |
279	| PUT | `/v1/uploads/{session}?offset=<n>` | 200 `{"offset":<confirmed length>}`; body holds the raw chunk bytes and `offset` must be a unique non-negative decimal integer | 400 invalid/truncated framing, 404 unknown or aborted session, 409 gap/overlap/overflow/conflict/empty-chunk/completed, 411 missing/non-integer/negative Content-Length, 405, 500 upload io error |
280	| POST | `/v1/uploads/{session}/complete` | 200 `{"sha256","size","content_type"}` (the first result on repeat completion); no body required | 404 unknown or aborted session, 409 incomplete or hash mismatch, 412 saved precondition failed, 400 bad framing, 405, 500 blob/upload io error |
281	| DELETE | `/v1/uploads/{session}` | 204 no body; aborts the session and keeps any published object | 404 unknown or aborted session, 405 |
282	
283	Notes:
284	
285	* `PUT` reads exactly `Content-Length` bytes from the request body; chunked
286	  request bodies are not supported.
287	* `after` is an exclusive lower bound on the key, so the `next_after` value of a
288	  page can be passed straight back as `after` to fetch the next page.
289	* `limit` must be an integer between 1 and 1000.
290	* Deleting a key removes only the metadata entry; blob bytes remain on disk
291	  because other keys may still reference the same digest. Run `gc` (preview by
292	  default, `gc --execute` to delete) to remove the blobs no object references.
293	  The success line is
294	  `{"ok":true,"digests":[...],"bytes":<int>,"dry_run":<bool>}`.
295	
296	Upload session notes:
297	
298	* `POST /v1/uploads` validates exactly like `begin_upload`: `key` is a
299	  non-empty slash-separated name without `.`/`..` parts or NUL bytes, `size`
300	  a non-negative JSON integer (booleans rejected), `sha256` 64 lowercase hex
301	  digits, and `content_type` a string when present. Extra fields are rejected.
302	  Creating a session never creates or changes an object.
303	* `PUT` appends follow the same rules as `append_upload`: a chunk must start
304	  at the current received end and may not run past the declared size; a chunk
305	  fully inside the received range succeeds at 200 without growing progress
306	  when its bytes match and gets 409 otherwise; empty chunks are accepted only
307	  at the current end. The 200 body always reports the confirmed length.
308	* Completing publishes the object only when the received length and the
309	  SHA-256 of the full content match (zero-byte objects included); repeating
310	  completion of the same session returns the first result without
311	  overwriting later writes or deletes of the key. Sessions on the same key
312	  publish in completion order; aborting a session keeps the object it
313	  published.
314	* `If-Match: "<sha256>"` or `If-None-Match: *` on `POST /v1/uploads` saves a
315	  condition exactly like `begin_upload(expected_sha256=...)`: it is not
316	  evaluated while the session is created or appended to, but once at
317	  completion, atomically with the publish and after the length/hash checks.
318	  Failure is `412 {"error":"precondition failed"}`, leaves the confirmed
319	  bytes and incomplete session usable, and remains in force after a restart.
320	* Session state lives in the same on-disk files as the Python API, so a
321	  session created through one entry can be appended to, completed, inspected
322	  or aborted through the other, and progress survives a server restart.
323	* Session requests are framed strictly by `Content-Length`; chunked request
324	  bodies are never accepted. A `GET`/`DELETE` status or abort call needs no
325	  body, but any `Content-Length` it sends must be a valid non-negative
326	  decimal integer and the declared bytes are consumed.
327	
328	## Storage layout
329	
330	```
331	<data-dir>/
332	  index.json            # {"version":1,"objects":{"<key>":{"sha256","size","content_type"}},
333	                        #  "tenants":{"<tenant>":{"<key>":{...}}} (non-default tenants,
334	                        #  only while non-empty),
335	                        #  "uploads":{"<session>":{"key","entry","tenant"?}} (only while non-empty)}
336	  blobs/<sha256>        # raw object bytes, one file per distinct digest
337	  uploads/<session>.json  # active upload declaration plus confirmed offset, tenant
338	                          # (non-default only) and optional expected_sha256 publish
339	                          # condition (lazy directory)
340	  uploads/<session>.part  # received bytes of an active upload
341	```
342	
343	The flat `objects` map holds the `default` tenant, so indexes written before
344	tenants existed need no migration; the same applies to session files and
345	completion records without a `tenant` field.
346	
347	## Limits of this seed
348	
349	The following long-term goals are intentionally not implemented yet: object
350	versioning and retention policies, lifecycle policies on top of the existing
351	garbage collection of unreferenced blobs, quotas and rate limiting, consistent
352	hashing and rebalancing, erasure coding and repair, signed URLs and access
353	control, cross-region replication and end-to-end audit logging. Resumable
354	uploads are exposed through the Python API and the HTTP surface; the command
355	line interface does not expose them yet. Authentication is out of scope: the
356	server trusts every caller.
357

# solo06 - Multi-Tenant Content-Addressed Object Store

This repository is a small but real backend skeleton for multi-tenant object
storage with content addressing. Every object key maps to the SHA-256 digest of
its bytes, blobs are written once under `<data-dir>/blobs/<sha256>` so identical
payloads are deduplicated no matter how many keys reference them, and object
metadata is kept in `<data-dir>/index.json` and rewritten atomically (temporary
file plus `os.replace`) so a crash never leaves a half-written index behind. The
same core is exposed three ways: as a Python API (`ContentAddressedStore`), as a
standard-library HTTP service, and as a command line tool. It uses only the
Python standard library, needs no network access and behaves deterministically,
which makes it a suitable frozen baseline for later work on chunked and
resumable uploads, object versioning and retention, lifecycle and garbage
collection, metadata indexing and listing, quotas and rate limiting, consistent
hashing and rebalancing, erasure coding and repair, signed URLs and access
control, cross-region replication and end-to-end audit.

## Requirements

* Python 3.10 or newer (developed and verified on Python 3.12).
* No third-party packages, no network access required.

## Usage

Start the HTTP server (run from the repository root):

```
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
```

The server prints one line of JSON before it starts serving, for example
`{"addr":"127.0.0.1:8080","data_dir":"/abs/path/objstore_data","ok":true}`, and
then runs until it receives SIGINT or SIGTERM.

Store and fetch data over HTTP:

```
printf 'hello' | curl -sS -X PUT --data-binary @- -H 'Content-Type: text/plain' \
  http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects/a.txt
curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects/a.txt
curl -sS 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/objects?prefix=&limit=100'
```

Upload a large payload through a resumable HTTP session:

```
size=$(wc -c < big.bin)
digest=$(sha256sum big.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
session=$(curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads \
  -d "{\"key\":\"docs/big.bin\",\"size\":$size,\"sha256\":\"$digest\"}" \
  | sed 's/.*"session":"\([0-9a-f]*\)".*/\1')
head -c 1048576 big.bin | curl -sS -X PUT \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session?offset=0" --data-binary @-
tail -c +1048577 big.bin | curl -sS -X PUT \
  "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session?offset=1048576" --data-binary @-
curl -sS -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/uploads/$session/complete"
```

Use the command line interface instead of the server:

```
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data put --key docs/a.txt --file ./a.txt
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data get --key docs/a.txt --out ./copy.txt
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data list --prefix docs/ --limit 100
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data delete --key docs/a.txt
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data gc
python3 -m objstore --data-dir ./objstore_data gc --execute
```

The global `--data-dir` option must appear before the subcommand; it defaults to
`./objstore_data`. `put`, `get`, `list` and `delete` also accept `--tenant`
(default `default`) to pick the tenant namespace. Every command prints exactly
one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0 on success, or prints one line of JSON
on stderr and exits non-zero on failure.

Use the Python API directly:

```python
from objstore import ContentAddressedStore

store = ContentAddressedStore("./objstore_data")
entry = store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", content_type="text/plain")
payload, head = store.get("docs/a.txt")
page = store.list_objects(prefix="docs/", after=None, limit=100)
result = store.collect_garbage()              # preview only
store.collect_garbage(dry_run=False)          # actually delete
```

### Tenants

Every object key lives in a tenant namespace. Two tenants may use the same
key for independent objects: reads, writes, deletes, conditional writes and
listings of one tenant never see or affect another tenant's objects. Tenants
need no provisioning — a tenant exists as soon as it has objects or sessions,
and listing a tenant without objects returns an empty page. A tenant name is
1–64 characters of lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`, starting with a
letter or digit; anything else raises `ObjectStoreError("invalid tenant: ...")`
(Python), returns `400 {"error":"invalid tenant ..."}` (HTTP) or the usual
CLI failure line with a non-zero exit, and changes no data.

The Python API takes an optional `tenant` keyword (default `"default"`) on
`put`, `get`, `head`, `delete`, `list_objects` and every upload-session
operation:

```python
store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", tenant="acme")
payload, head = store.get("docs/a.txt", tenant="acme")
page = store.list_objects(prefix="docs/", tenant="acme")
session = store.begin_upload("docs/big.bin", size, digest, tenant="acme")
```

The HTTP object and upload-session endpoints select the tenant through the
optional `X-Objstore-Tenant` request header (default `default`); a repeated
header or an invalid name returns `400 {"error":"invalid tenant ..."}` and
takes precedence over every other request error. The CLI commands `put`,
`get`, `list` and `delete` accept an optional `--tenant` flag.

A conditional write compares only the digest of the key in the same tenant,
and an upload session belongs to the tenant fixed at creation: its status,
append, complete and abort operations must name that tenant, and a valid
session id of another tenant behaves exactly like an unknown session id
(`ObjectStoreError` / `404`) without revealing any state. Blobs stay global —
identical content is stored once across all tenants, `blob`/`blob_digests`
and `GET /v1/blobs/{sha256}` keep their global meaning, and garbage
collection only reclaims content no tenant references anymore. Directories
written by older versions (objects, sessions and completion records without
tenant information) belong to the `default` tenant after the upgrade.

### Conditional writes

`put`, `delete` and `begin_upload` take an optional keyword
`expected_sha256` that makes the write or delete an atomic compare-and-swap on
the target key's current digest:

* omitted entirely keeps the original unconditional behaviour;
* an explicit `None` requires the key not to exist;
* a string of 64 lowercase hex digits requires the key to exist with exactly
  that metadata digest.

Only that key's digest is compared; the content type and every other key are
irrelevant. Any other value raises
`ObjectStoreError("invalid precondition")`. When the condition does not hold,
the operation raises `ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")` and changes
neither the object nor (for uploads) the session progress or any blob; a
satisfied absent-condition `delete` still raises the usual
`ObjectStoreError("not found: ...")`. The check and the mutation are one
indivisible operation under the store lock, so two concurrent writes that
both expect the same old digest cannot both succeed.

```python
store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello", expected_sha256=None)          # create only
store.put("docs/a.txt", b"hello!", expected_sha256=head["sha256"])  # CAS update
store.delete("docs/a.txt", expected_sha256=head["sha256"])      # delete if unchanged
```

For a resumable session the condition passed to `begin_upload` is saved with
the session and is not checked while the session is created or appended to;
it is evaluated once, atomically with the publish, against the object's state
at completion time (after the length and hash checks pass). A failed
precondition leaves the confirmed bytes and the incomplete session in place,
so it can be completed again or aborted; the condition still applies after
reopening the data directory, while session files written by older versions
stay unconditional.

### Resumable uploads

Large or unreliable transfers can be uploaded in chunks through a persistent
session instead of a single `put`:

```python
session = store.begin_upload("docs/big.bin", size, sha256_of_full_content,
                             content_type="application/octet-stream")
store.upload_status(session)          # {"key","size","sha256","content_type","offset","completed"}
store.append_upload(session, 0, first_chunk)      # returns the received length
store.append_upload(session, len(first_chunk), second_chunk)
entry = store.complete_upload(session)            # publishes, returns put metadata
store.abort_upload(session)                       # or drop the session entirely
```

`begin_upload` validates the key and content type exactly like `put`, requires
a non-negative integer `size` (booleans excluded) and the 64 lowercase hex
digits of the full content's SHA-256, and returns a unique string session id.
Creating a session changes no object, and sessions with their confirmed
progress survive reopening the data directory. `append_upload` accepts the
same byte types as `put`: a new chunk must start exactly at the current end
and may not exceed the declared size; re-sending identical bytes fully inside
the received range succeeds without growing, while different bytes, chunks
overlapping the received end, gaps and empty chunks anywhere but at the end
all raise `ObjectStoreError`. `complete_upload` publishes the object only when
the received length and the SHA-256 of the full content match the declaration
(zero-byte objects included); until then the key keeps its old value and no
new blob appears. Appending after completion fails, repeating a completed
`complete_upload` returns the first result without overwriting later writes
or deletes of the key, and `abort_upload` removes the session (returning
`None`) without deleting any published object. An interrupted append leaves
either the old progress or a whole new chunk, and an interrupted complete
leaves either the old object or the fully published new one; after recovery
the `completed` flag always agrees with what was published. Sessions on the
same key are independent and publish in completion order. Garbage collection
never touches data needed by incomplete sessions; once a session completes or
is aborted, its blob follows the normal object-reference rules and the
completion record itself keeps nothing alive. The command line interface is
unchanged by this feature; the HTTP session surface is documented below.

`collect_garbage(dry_run=True)` returns
`{"digests": [...], "bytes": <int>, "dry_run": <bool>}`: the digests sorted
lexicographically and the sum of the files' actual byte sizes (zero-byte
blobs included). A dry run reports the candidates and changes nothing;
`dry_run=False` deletes the candidates and reports what that call removed.
References are recomputed from the current index on every call, so content
still shared by any key is kept, while content orphaned by an overwrite, by
deleting the last reference, or never indexed at all is collectable. Only
regular files directly in `blobs/` whose names are 64 lowercase hex digits
are eligible; other names, temporary files, subdirectories and symlinks are
preserved and symlink targets are never followed. Unreferenced files are
deleted without validating their content, and missing or corrupted blobs
that are still referenced do not block other candidates. A non-boolean
`dry_run` raises `ObjectStoreError("invalid dry_run")`, and any scanning,
stating or deletion I/O failure raises `ObjectStoreError("gc io error")`; a
failed scan deletes nothing, and a failure mid-deletion leaves the completed
deletions in place so a retry collects the rest. Garbage collection runs
under the same lock as object reads and writes within one store instance.


## Tests

```
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Run the command from the repository root so that `import objstore` resolves.

## HTTP API

Errors are always JSON: `{"error": "..."}`. Unknown keys return
`404 {"error":"not found"}`; a malformed digest returns
`400 {"error":"invalid sha256"}`; an out-of-range or non-numeric `limit`
returns `400 {"error":"invalid limit"}`; an unknown path returns
`404 {"error":"not found"}`. Object PUT/DELETE and `POST /v1/uploads` accept
conditional headers: `If-Match` must be a single double-quoted lowercase
digest (`If-Match: "<sha256>"`) requiring the key to hold that digest, and
`If-None-Match: *` requires the key to be absent. Both headers together, a
repeated header, or any other value returns
`400 {"error":"invalid precondition"}`; a condition that does not hold
returns `412 {"error":"precondition failed"}` without changing anything (an
absent-key `DELETE` still returns its `404 not found`). Request/body errors,
unknown sessions, and length/hash conflicts keep their usual status codes and
take precedence over the condition. Successful object GET and HEAD return an
`ETag` header holding the current digest in double quotes; no other success
response changes. Upload session conflicts (gaps, bytes past the
received end or the declared size, conflicting re-sends, empty chunks away
from the end, appending after completion, or completing with the wrong length
or hash) return `409` and never change progress or the target object; a
missing, non-integer or negative `Content-Length` on session creation or
chunk append returns `411 {"error":"length required"}`; a request carrying
`Transfer-Encoding` returns `400` and a body shorter than its declared
`Content-Length` also returns `400`. Every object GET and blob GET recomputes
the SHA-256 of the bytes actually on disk before serving them; object GET also
checks the byte count against the metadata `size`. A failed check returns
`500 {"error":"corrupted blob"}` with no object bytes, and an I/O error on an
existing blob returns `500 {"error":"blob io error"}`; upload session I/O
failures return `500 {"error":"upload io error"}`. Re-PUTting an object
whose digest file is corrupted restores that file atomically from the complete
request body, which also repairs every other key sharing that digest; HEAD,
listings and digest listings remain metadata-only and perform no content
checks.

| Method | Path | Success | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/healthz` | 200 `{"ok": true}` | 405 |
| PUT | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 201 `{"key","sha256","size"}` on first store; 200 with the same body when the same bytes are stored again | 400 invalid key / invalid precondition, 411 missing Content-Length, 405, 412 precondition failed, 500 blob io error |
| GET | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 200 raw bytes, headers `Content-Type`, `X-Content-Sha256` and `ETag` (`"<sha256>"`) | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key, 405, 500 corrupted blob / blob io error |
| HEAD | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 200 no body, headers `Content-Length`, `X-Content-Sha256` and `ETag` | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key, 405 |
| DELETE | `/v1/objects/{key}` | 204 no body | 404 unknown key, 400 invalid key / invalid precondition, 405, 412 precondition failed |
| GET | `/v1/objects?prefix=&after=&limit=` | 200 `{"items":[{"key","sha256","size","content_type"}],"next_after":<str or null>}` | 400 invalid limit, 400 invalid prefix, 400 invalid after, 405 |
| GET | `/v1/blobs/{sha256}` | 200 raw bytes of that content, header `X-Content-Sha256` | 400 invalid sha256, 404 unknown digest, 405, 500 corrupted blob / blob io error |
| POST | `/v1/uploads` | 201 `{"session":"<id>"}`; body is a UTF-8 JSON object with required `key`, `size`, `sha256` and optional `content_type` (default `null`); optional `If-Match`/`If-None-Match` save a publish-time condition | 400 invalid json / fields / invalid precondition, 411 missing/non-integer/negative Content-Length, 400 Transfer-Encoding / truncated body, 405, 500 upload io error |
| GET | `/v1/uploads/{session}` | 200 `{"key","size","sha256","content_type","offset","completed"}` | 404 unknown or aborted session, 405 |
| PUT | `/v1/uploads/{session}?offset=<n>` | 200 `{"offset":<confirmed length>}`; body holds the raw chunk bytes and `offset` must be a unique non-negative decimal integer | 400 invalid/truncated framing, 404 unknown or aborted session, 409 gap/overlap/overflow/conflict/empty-chunk/completed, 411 missing/non-integer/negative Content-Length, 405, 500 upload io error |
| POST | `/v1/uploads/{session}/complete` | 200 `{"sha256","size","content_type"}` (the first result on repeat completion); no body required | 404 unknown or aborted session, 409 incomplete or hash mismatch, 412 saved precondition failed, 400 bad framing, 405, 500 blob/upload io error |
| DELETE | `/v1/uploads/{session}` | 204 no body; aborts the session and keeps any published object | 404 unknown or aborted session, 405 |

Notes:

* `PUT` reads exactly `Content-Length` bytes from the request body; chunked
  request bodies are not supported.
* `after` is an exclusive lower bound on the key, so the `next_after` value of a
  page can be passed straight back as `after` to fetch the next page.
* `limit` must be an integer between 1 and 1000.
* Deleting a key removes only the metadata entry; blob bytes remain on disk
  because other keys may still reference the same digest. Run `gc` (preview by
  default, `gc --execute` to delete) to remove the blobs no object references.
  The success line is
  `{"ok":true,"digests":[...],"bytes":<int>,"dry_run":<bool>}`.

Upload session notes:

* `POST /v1/uploads` validates exactly like `begin_upload`: `key` is a
  non-empty slash-separated name without `.`/`..` parts or NUL bytes, `size`
  a non-negative JSON integer (booleans rejected), `sha256` 64 lowercase hex
  digits, and `content_type` a string when present. Extra fields are rejected.
  Creating a session never creates or changes an object.
* `PUT` appends follow the same rules as `append_upload`: a chunk must start
  at the current received end and may not run past the declared size; a chunk
  fully inside the received range succeeds at 200 without growing progress
  when its bytes match and gets 409 otherwise; empty chunks are accepted only
  at the current end. The 200 body always reports the confirmed length.
* Completing publishes the object only when the received length and the
  SHA-256 of the full content match (zero-byte objects included); repeating
  completion of the same session returns the first result without
  overwriting later writes or deletes of the key. Sessions on the same key
  publish in completion order; aborting a session keeps the object it
  published.
* `If-Match: "<sha256>"` or `If-None-Match: *` on `POST /v1/uploads` saves a
  condition exactly like `begin_upload(expected_sha256=...)`: it is not
  evaluated while the session is created or appended to, but once at
  completion, atomically with the publish and after the length/hash checks.
  Failure is `412 {"error":"precondition failed"}`, leaves the confirmed
  bytes and incomplete session usable, and remains in force after a restart.
* Session state lives in the same on-disk files as the Python API, so a
  session created through one entry can be appended to, completed, inspected
  or aborted through the other, and progress survives a server restart.
* Session requests are framed strictly by `Content-Length`; chunked request
  bodies are never accepted. A `GET`/`DELETE` status or abort call needs no
  body, but any `Content-Length` it sends must be a valid non-negative
  decimal integer and the declared bytes are consumed.

## Storage layout

```
<data-dir>/
  index.json            # {"version":1,"objects":{"<key>":{"sha256","size","content_type"}},
                        #  "tenants":{"<tenant>":{"<key>":{...}}} (non-default tenants,
                        #  only while non-empty),
                        #  "uploads":{"<session>":{"key","entry","tenant"?}} (only while non-empty)}
  blobs/<sha256>        # raw object bytes, one file per distinct digest
  uploads/<session>.json  # active upload declaration plus confirmed offset, tenant
                          # (non-default only) and optional expected_sha256 publish
                          # condition (lazy directory)
  uploads/<session>.part  # received bytes of an active upload
```

The flat `objects` map holds the `default` tenant, so indexes written before
tenants existed need no migration; the same applies to session files and
completion records without a `tenant` field.

## Limits of this seed

The following long-term goals are intentionally not implemented yet: object
versioning and retention policies, lifecycle policies on top of the existing
garbage collection of unreferenced blobs, quotas and rate limiting, consistent
hashing and rebalancing, erasure coding and repair, signed URLs and access
control, cross-region replication and end-to-end audit logging. Resumable
uploads are exposed through the Python API and the HTTP surface; the command
line interface does not expose them yet. Authentication is out of scope: the
server trusts every caller.

1	"""Content-addressed object store (standard library only).
2	
3	Blob bytes are stored once as ``<root>/blobs/<sha256>``; object metadata
4	(``key -> {sha256, size, content_type}``) lives in ``<root>/index.json`` and is
5	always rewritten through a temporary file plus ``os.replace``. Every mutation
6	and every consistent read runs under a single re-entrant lock.
7	
8	Objects are namespaced per tenant: every object and upload operation takes an
9	optional ``tenant`` keyword defaulting to ``"default"``, and the same key in
10	different tenants refers to independent objects. In the index the default
11	tenant keeps the historical flat ``objects`` map while other tenants are
12	stored under a ``tenants`` map, so directories written by older versions
13	silently belong to the default tenant. Blobs stay global: identical content
14	is stored once no matter which tenants reference it, and garbage collection
15	considers the references of every tenant.
16	
17	Resumable uploads live under ``<root>/uploads/`` (created lazily): each
18	session is a ``<session>.json`` declaration plus confirmed offset and a
19	``<session>.part`` file holding the received bytes. A session belongs to the
20	tenant fixed at creation; operations naming another tenant behave exactly as
21	if the session did not exist. Completing a session publishes the object in
22	the session's tenant and records the result in the index's ``uploads`` map in
23	one atomic index rewrite, so the completion flag can never disagree with the
24	published object.
25	"""
26	
27	from __future__ import annotations
28	
29	import hashlib
30	import json
31	import os
32	import re
33	import stat
34	import threading
35	import uuid
36	
37	__all__ = ["ContentAddressedStore", "ObjectStoreError", "SessionConflict"]
38	
39	INDEX_NAME = "index.json"
40	BLOBS_DIRNAME = "blobs"
41	UPLOADS_DIRNAME = "uploads"
42	INDEX_VERSION = 1
43	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 100
44	MAX_LIMIT = 1000
45	DEFAULT_TENANT = "default"
46	
47	_SHA256_RE = re.compile(r"\A[0-9a-f]{64}\Z")
48	_SESSION_META_RE = re.compile(r"\A([0-9a-f]{32})\.json\Z")
49	_TENANT_RE = re.compile(r"\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}\Z")
50	_MISSING = object()
51	
52	
53	class ObjectStoreError(Exception):
54	    """Missing object, invalid key/digest/limit, or a corrupted index."""
55	
56	
57	class SessionConflict(ObjectStoreError):
58	    """An upload operation that violates the session's current state.
59	
60	    A subclass of :class:`ObjectStoreError`, so existing callers keep
61	    catching it; front ends (HTTP) can nevertheless distinguish these
62	    state conflicts from bad input and report them separately.
63	    """
64	
65	
66	def _is_sha256(value):
67	    return isinstance(value, str) and _SHA256_RE.match(value) is not None
68	
69	
70	def _atomic_write(path, data):
71	    """Write *data* to *path* via a unique temp file plus os.replace."""
72	    tmp = "%s.tmp.%d.%d" % (path, os.getpid(), threading.get_ident())
73	    try:
74	        with open(tmp, "wb") as handle:
75	            handle.write(data)
76	            handle.flush()
77	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
78	        os.replace(tmp, path)
79	    finally:
80	        if os.path.exists(tmp):
81	            try:
82	                os.remove(tmp)
83	            except OSError:
84	                pass
85	
86	
87	class ContentAddressedStore:
88	    """Multi-tenant key -> content-addressed blob mapping persisted on disk."""
89	
90	    def __init__(self, root):
91	        if not isinstance(root, (str, bytes, os.PathLike)):
92	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid root: %r" % (root,))
93	        self.root = os.path.abspath(os.fspath(root))
94	        self.blobs_dir = os.path.join(self.root, BLOBS_DIRNAME)
95	        self.uploads_dir = os.path.join(self.root, UPLOADS_DIRNAME)
96	        self.index_path = os.path.join(self.root, INDEX_NAME)
97	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
98	        os.makedirs(self.blobs_dir, exist_ok=True)
99	        self._objects, self._upload_records = self._load_index()
100	        self._uploads = self._load_uploads()
101	
102	    # -- index ---------------------------------------------------------
103	    def _load_index(self):
104	        if not os.path.exists(self.index_path):
105	            return {DEFAULT_TENANT: {}}, {}
106	        try:
107	            with open(self.index_path, "rb") as handle:
108	                document = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))
109	        except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
110	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: %s" % (exc,))
111	        if not isinstance(document, dict) or not isinstance(document.get("objects"), dict):
112	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: missing objects map")
113	        objects = {DEFAULT_TENANT: self._load_object_map(document["objects"])}
114	        raw_tenants = document.get("tenants", {})
115	        if not isinstance(raw_tenants, dict):
116	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: tenants is not a map")
117	        for tenant, mapping in raw_tenants.items():
118	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or tenant == DEFAULT_TENANT \
119	                    or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
120	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad tenant")
121	            if not isinstance(mapping, dict):
122	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad tenant objects")
123	            objects[tenant] = self._load_object_map(mapping)
124	        records = {}
125	        raw_records = document.get("uploads", {})
126	        if not isinstance(raw_records, dict):
127	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: uploads is not a map")
128	        for session_id, record in raw_records.items():
129	            if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not isinstance(record, dict):
130	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad upload record")
131	            key = record.get("key")
132	            if not isinstance(key, str):
133	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad upload record")
134	            tenant = record.get("tenant", DEFAULT_TENANT)
135	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
136	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad upload record")
137	            records[session_id] = {
138	                "key": key,
139	                "entry": self._validate_entry(key, record.get("entry")),
140	                "tenant": tenant,
141	            }
142	        return objects, records
143	
144	    def _load_object_map(self, mapping):
145	        objects = {}
146	        for key, entry in mapping.items():
147	            if not isinstance(key, str):
148	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: non-string key")
149	            objects[key] = self._validate_entry(key, entry)
150	        return objects

152	    @staticmethod
153	    def _validate_entry(key, entry):
154	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
155	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: entry for %r is not an object" % (key,))
156	        sha, size = entry.get("sha256"), entry.get("size")
157	        content_type = entry.get("content_type")
158	        if not _is_sha256(sha):
159	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad sha256 for %r" % (key,))
160	        if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
161	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad size for %r" % (key,))
162	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
163	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted index: bad content_type for %r" % (key,))
164	        return {"sha256": sha, "size": size, "content_type": content_type}

166	    def _save_index(self):
167	        document = {"version": INDEX_VERSION,
168	                    "objects": self._objects.get(DEFAULT_TENANT, {})}
169	        tenants = {tenant: mapping for tenant, mapping in self._objects.items()
170	                   if tenant != DEFAULT_TENANT and mapping}
171	        if tenants:
172	            document["tenants"] = tenants
173	        if self._upload_records:
174	            records = {}
175	            for session_id, record in self._upload_records.items():
176	                saved = {"key": record["key"], "entry": record["entry"]}
177	                if record["tenant"] != DEFAULT_TENANT:
178	                    saved["tenant"] = record["tenant"]
179	                records[session_id] = saved
180	            document["uploads"] = records
181	        payload = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
182	        _atomic_write(self.index_path, payload.encode("utf-8") + b"\n")

184	    # -- validation ----------------------------------------------------
185	    @staticmethod
186	    def _check_tenant(tenant):
187	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
188	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid tenant: %r" % (tenant,))

191	    @staticmethod
192	    def _check_key(key):
193	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key or "\x00" in key:
194	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid key: %r" % (key,))
195	        if any(part in ("", ".", "..") for part in key.split("/")):
196	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid key: %r" % (key,))

199	    @staticmethod
200	    def _check_limit(limit):
201	        if isinstance(limit, bool) or not isinstance(limit, int):
202	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid limit: %r" % (limit,))
203	        if not 1 <= limit <= MAX_LIMIT:
204	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid limit: %r" % (limit,))

207	    @staticmethod
208	    def _require_sha(sha256):
209	        if not _is_sha256(sha256):
210	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid sha256: %r" % (sha256,))
211	        return sha256

213	    @staticmethod
214	    def _check_precondition(expected_sha256):
215	        """Normalize an ``expected_sha256`` keyword argument.
216	
217	        Omitted (the ``_MISSING`` sentinel) means no condition; an explicit
218	        ``None`` means the key must not exist; a 64-digit lowercase hex string
219	        means the key must exist with that exact digest. Anything else is an
220	        ``invalid precondition`` error rather than a failed condition.
221	        """
222	        if expected_sha256 is _MISSING:
223	            return _MISSING
224	        if expected_sha256 is None:
225	            return None
226	        if _is_sha256(expected_sha256):
227	            return expected_sha256
228	        raise ObjectStoreError("invalid precondition")
229	
230	    def _precondition_met(self, tenant, key, expected):
231	        """Return whether *key* in *tenant* currently satisfies *expected*."""
232	        entry = self._objects.get(tenant, {}).get(key)
233	        if expected is None:
234	            return entry is None
235	        return entry is not None and entry["sha256"] == expected

237	    # -- object API ----------------------------------------------------
238	    def put(self, key, payload, content_type=None, expected_sha256=_MISSING,
239	            tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
240	        """Store *payload* under *key* in *tenant* and return its metadata.
241	
242	        *expected_sha256* is an atomic precondition on the key's current
243	        digest in the same tenant: omitted leaves the old overwrite
244	        behaviour, an explicit ``None`` requires the key not to exist, and a
245	        64 lowercase hex digest requires the key to exist with exactly that
246	        digest. Content type and other keys are not compared. Objects of
247	        other tenants are never consulted or touched.
248	        """
249	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
250	        self._check_key(key)
251	        if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
252	            raise ObjectStoreError("payload must be bytes")
253	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
254	            raise ObjectStoreError("content_type must be a string or None")
255	        expected = self._check_precondition(expected_sha256)
256	        data = bytes(payload)
257	        sha = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
258	        entry = {"sha256": sha, "size": len(data), "content_type": content_type}
259	        with self._lock:
260	            if expected is not _MISSING and not self._precondition_met(
261	                    tenant, key, expected):
262	                raise ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")
263	            self._store_blob(sha, data)
264	            self._objects.setdefault(tenant, {})[key] = entry
265	            self._save_index()
266	            return dict(entry)
267	
268	    def _store_blob(self, sha, data):
269	        """Write the blob for *sha* when missing and repair it when corrupted.
270	
271	        An existing file is hashed on every put. Intact files are left exactly
272	        as they are so dedup costs nothing extra; a file whose digest no longer
273	        matches is rewritten atomically from the complete *data*, so an
274	        interrupted repair leaves either the old bytes or the full new bytes.
275	        """
276	        path = os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, sha)
277	        if os.path.exists(path):
278	            try:
279	                with open(path, "rb") as handle:
280	                    stored = handle.read()
281	            except FileNotFoundError:
282	                stored = None
283	            except OSError:
284	                raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
285	            if stored is not None:
286	                if hashlib.sha256(stored).hexdigest() == sha:
287	                    return
288	                try:
289	                    _atomic_write(path, data)
290	                except OSError:
291	                    raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
292	                return
293	        try:
294	            _atomic_write(path, data)
295	        except OSError:
296	            raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
297	
298	    def get(self, key, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
299	        """Return ``(payload, entry)`` for *key* in *tenant*."""
300	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
301	        with self._lock:
302	            entry = self.head(key, tenant=tenant)
303	            data = self.blob(entry["sha256"])
304	            if len(data) != entry["size"]:
305	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted blob")
306	            return data, entry

308	    def head(self, key, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
309	        """Return a copy of the metadata entry for *key* in *tenant*."""
310	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
311	        self._check_key(key)
312	        with self._lock:
313	            entry = self._objects.get(tenant, {}).get(key)
314	            if entry is None:
315	                raise ObjectStoreError("not found: %s" % (key,))
316	            return dict(entry)

318	    def delete(self, key, expected_sha256=_MISSING, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
319	        """Drop *key* in *tenant*; shared blobs stay on disk for other keys.
320	
321	        With *expected_sha256*, deletion also requires the key's current
322	        digest in this tenant to match (or an explicit ``None`` requires the
323	        key absent); a satisfied absent-condition delete still reports the
324	        key as not found. Objects other tenants keep under the same key are
325	        unaffected.
326	        """
327	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
328	        self._check_key(key)
329	        expected = self._check_precondition(expected_sha256)
330	        with self._lock:
331	            objects = self._objects.get(tenant, {})
332	            if key not in objects:
333	                raise ObjectStoreError("not found: %s" % (key,))
334	            if expected is not _MISSING and not self._precondition_met(
335	                    tenant, key, expected):
336	                raise ObjectStoreError("precondition failed")
337	            del objects[key]
338	            self._save_index()

340	    def blob(self, sha256):
341	        """Return the raw bytes stored under digest *sha256*.
342	
343	        The digest of the bytes actually on disk is recomputed on every read,
344	        so truncation, appended bytes and same-length tampering are all
345	        rejected instead of being handed back to the caller.
346	        """
347	        self._require_sha(sha256)
348	        with self._lock:
349	            try:
350	                with open(os.path.join(self.blobs_dir, sha256), "rb") as handle:
351	                    data = handle.read()
352	            except FileNotFoundError:
353	                raise ObjectStoreError("not found: blob %s" % (sha256,))
354	            except OSError:
355	                raise ObjectStoreError("blob io error")
356	            if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != sha256:
357	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted blob")
358	            return data
359	
360	    def blob_digests(self):
361	        """Return the sorted digests currently present in the blob directory."""
362	        with self._lock:
363	            return sorted(name for name in os.listdir(self.blobs_dir) if _is_sha256(name))

365	    # -- resumable uploads ----------------------------------------------
366	    def _session_meta_path(self, session_id):
367	        return os.path.join(self.uploads_dir, session_id + ".json")
368	
369	    def _session_part_path(self, session_id):
370	        return os.path.join(self.uploads_dir, session_id + ".part")
371	
372	    def _load_uploads(self):
373	        uploads = {}
374	        try:
375	            names = os.listdir(self.uploads_dir)
376	        except FileNotFoundError:
377	            return uploads
378	        except OSError:
379	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
380	        for name in sorted(names):
381	            match = _SESSION_META_RE.match(name)
382	            if match is None:
383	                continue
384	            session_id = match.group(1)
385	            if session_id in self._upload_records:
386	                # completed before a crash could clean its files up
387	                self._discard_session_files(session_id)
388	                continue
389	            session = self._read_session_meta(session_id)
390	            self._check_part_file(session_id, session["offset"])
391	            uploads[session_id] = session
392	        return uploads

394	    def _read_session_meta(self, session_id):
395	        try:
396	            with open(self._session_meta_path(session_id), "rb") as handle:
397	                document = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))
398	        except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
399	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: %s" % (exc,))
400	        if not isinstance(document, dict):
401	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: not an object")
402	        key = document.get("key")
403	        size = document.get("size")
404	        sha = document.get("sha256")
405	        content_type = document.get("content_type")
406	        offset = document.get("offset")
407	        expected = document.get("expected_sha256", _MISSING)
408	        tenant = document.get("tenant", DEFAULT_TENANT)
409	        try:
410	            self._check_key(key)
411	        except ObjectStoreError:
412	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad key")
413	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or _TENANT_RE.match(tenant) is None:
414	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad tenant")
415	        if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
416	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad size")
417	        if not _is_sha256(sha):
418	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad sha256")
419	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
420	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad content_type")
421	        if isinstance(offset, bool) or not isinstance(offset, int) or not 0 <= offset <= size:
422	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad offset")
423	        # Sessions written by older versions have no condition; an explicit
424	        # null requires the key absent, a string requires that digest.
425	        if expected is not _MISSING and expected is not None and not _is_sha256(expected):
426	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: bad precondition")
427	        return {"key": key, "size": size, "sha256": sha,
428	                "content_type": content_type, "offset": offset,
429	                "expected_sha256": expected, "tenant": tenant}

431	    def _check_part_file(self, session_id, offset):
432	        """Ensure the part file holds exactly the confirmed *offset* bytes.
433	
434	        A crash between the chunk write and the metadata update can leave
435	        unconfirmed bytes behind; they are truncated so recovery sees either
436	        the old progress or a whole confirmed chunk, never a partial one.
437	        """
438	        path = self._session_part_path(session_id)
439	        try:
440	            size_on_disk = os.stat(path).st_size
441	        except FileNotFoundError:
442	            if offset:
443	                raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: missing data")
444	            try:
445	                with open(path, "wb"):
446	                    pass
447	            except OSError:
448	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
449	            return
450	        except OSError:
451	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
452	        if size_on_disk < offset:
453	            raise ObjectStoreError("corrupted upload session: truncated data")
454	        if size_on_disk > offset:
455	            try:
456	                with open(path, "r+b") as handle:
457	                    handle.truncate(offset)
458	                    handle.flush()
459	                    os.fsync(handle.fileno())
460	            except OSError:
461	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
462	
463	    def _save_session(self, session_id, session):
464	        # The default tenant is implicit so older session files stay
465	        # byte-identical; every other tenant is recorded explicitly.
466	        document = {name: value for name, value in session.items()
467	                    if value is not _MISSING
468	                    and not (name == "tenant" and value == DEFAULT_TENANT)}
469	        payload = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
470	        try:
471	            _atomic_write(self._session_meta_path(session_id),
472	                          payload.encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
473	        except OSError:
474	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
475	
476	    def _write_part(self, session_id, offset, data):
477	        try:
478	            with open(self._session_part_path(session_id), "r+b") as handle:
479	                handle.seek(offset)
480	                handle.write(data)
481	                handle.flush()
482	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
483	        except OSError:
484	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
485	
486	    def _read_part(self, session_id, offset, length):
487	        try:
488	            with open(self._session_part_path(session_id), "rb") as handle:
489	                handle.seek(offset)
490	                return handle.read(length)
491	        except OSError:
492	            raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
493	
494	    def _remove_session_files(self, session_id):
495	        for path in (self._session_meta_path(session_id),
496	                     self._session_part_path(session_id)):
497	            try:
498	                os.remove(path)
499	            except FileNotFoundError:
500	                pass
501	            except OSError:
502	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
503	        self._tidy_uploads_dir()
504	
505	    def _discard_session_files(self, session_id):
506	        for path in (self._session_meta_path(session_id),
507	                     self._session_part_path(session_id)):
508	            try:
509	                os.remove(path)
510	            except OSError:
511	                pass
512	        self._tidy_uploads_dir()
513	
514	    def _tidy_uploads_dir(self):
515	        try:
516	            os.rmdir(self.uploads_dir)
517	        except OSError:
518	            pass

520	    def _new_session_id(self):
521	        while True:
522	            session_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
523	            if session_id in self._uploads or session_id in self._upload_records:
524	                continue
525	            if os.path.exists(self._session_meta_path(session_id)):
526	                continue
527	            return session_id

529	    @staticmethod
530	    def _check_session_id(session_id):
531	        if not isinstance(session_id, str) or not session_id:
532	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
533	        return session_id
534	
535	    def _require_active_session(self, session_id, tenant):
536	        self._check_session_id(session_id)
537	        record = self._upload_records.get(session_id)
538	        if record is not None and record["tenant"] == tenant:
539	            raise SessionConflict(
540	                "upload session already completed: %s" % (session_id,))
541	        session = self._uploads.get(session_id)
542	        if session is None or session["tenant"] != tenant:
543	            # Sessions of other tenants are indistinguishable from unknown
544	            # ones: no state or progress leaks across tenant boundaries.
545	            raise ObjectStoreError("unknown upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
546	        return session

548	    def begin_upload(self, key, size, sha256, content_type=None,
549	                     expected_sha256=_MISSING, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
550	        """Start a resumable upload session and return its unique id.
551	
552	        The key and content type follow the same rules as :meth:`put`, *size*
553	        must be a non-negative integer (booleans excluded) and *sha256* the
554	        64 lowercase hex digits of the full content's digest. Creating a
555	        session changes no object; the session and its progress survive
556	        reopening the data directory. The session belongs to *tenant* for its
557	        whole lifetime: every later operation must name the same tenant.
558	
559	        *expected_sha256* saves the same kind of precondition as :meth:`put`;
560	        it is checked once, atomically with the publish, when the session
561	        completes, never while the session is created or appended to.
562	        """
563	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
564	        self._check_key(key)
565	        if isinstance(size, bool) or not isinstance(size, int) or size < 0:
566	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid size: %r" % (size,))
567	        self._require_sha(sha256)
568	        if content_type is not None and not isinstance(content_type, str):
569	            raise ObjectStoreError("content_type must be a string or None")
570	        expected = self._check_precondition(expected_sha256)
571	        session = {"key": key, "size": size, "sha256": sha256,
572	                   "content_type": content_type, "offset": 0,
573	                   "expected_sha256": expected, "tenant": tenant}
574	        with self._lock:
575	            session_id = self._new_session_id()
576	            try:
577	                os.makedirs(self.uploads_dir, exist_ok=True)
578	                with open(self._session_part_path(session_id), "wb"):
579	                    pass
580	            except OSError:
581	                raise ObjectStoreError("upload io error")
582	            try:
583	                self._save_session(session_id, session)
584	            except ObjectStoreError:
585	                self._discard_session_files(session_id)
586	                raise
587	            self._uploads[session_id] = session
588	            return session_id

590	    def upload_status(self, session_id, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
591	        """Return the declaration, received ``offset`` and ``completed`` flag.
592	
593	        Only the session's owning tenant sees it; every other tenant gets
594	        the same ``unknown upload session`` error as for a session that
595	        never existed.
596	        """
597	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
598	        self._check_session_id(session_id)
599	        with self._lock:
600	            record = self._upload_records.get(session_id)
601	            if record is not None:
602	                if record["tenant"] != tenant:
603	                    raise ObjectStoreError(
604	                        "unknown upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
605	                entry = record["entry"]
606	                return {"key": record["key"], "size": entry["size"],
607	                        "sha256": entry["sha256"],
608	                        "content_type": entry["content_type"],
609	                        "offset": entry["size"], "completed": True}
610	            session = self._uploads.get(session_id)
611	            if session is None or session["tenant"] != tenant:
612	                raise ObjectStoreError("unknown upload session: %r" % (session_id,))
613	            return {"key": session["key"], "size": session["size"],
614	                    "sha256": session["sha256"],
615	                    "content_type": session["content_type"],
616	                    "offset": session["offset"], "completed": False}

618	    def append_upload(self, session_id, offset, payload, tenant=DEFAULT_TENANT):
619	        """Append one chunk to *session_id* and return the received length.
620	
621	        A new chunk must start exactly at the current end and may not exceed
622	        the declared total size. A chunk lying fully inside the received
623	        range succeeds without growing when its bytes are identical to what
624	        is stored, and fails otherwise; chunks overlapping the end, chunks
625	        past the end and empty chunks anywhere but at the end all fail.
626	        """
627	        self._check_tenant(tenant)
628	        self._check_session_id(session_id)
629	        if isinstance(offset, bool) or not isinstance(offset, int) or offset < 0:
630	            raise ObjectStoreError("invalid offset: %r" % (offset,))
631	        if not isinstance(payload, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
632	            raise ObjectStoreError("payload must be bytes")
633	        data = bytes(payload)
634	        with self._lock:
635	            session = self._require_active_session(session_id, tenant)
636	            current = session["offset"]
637	            if offset > current:
638	                raise SessionConflict(
639	                    "append gap: offset %d beyond received %d" % (offset, current))
640	            if not data:
641	                if offset != current:
642	                    raise SessionConflict("empty chunk only at received end")
643	                return current
644	            end = offset + len(data)
645	            if offset < current:
646	                if end > current:
647	                    raise SessionConflict("append overlaps received end")
648	                if self._read_part(session_id, offset, len(data)) != data:
649	                    raise SessionConflict("append conflicts with received bytes")
650	                return current
651	            if end > session["size"]:
652	                raise SessionConflict("append exceeds declared size")
653	            self._write_part(session_id, offset, data)
654	            self._save_session(session_id, dict(session, offset=end))
655	            session["offset"] = end
656	            return end
